policy: Bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food is prohibited; handlers must use gloves, utensils, or deli tissue. Notwithstanding this rule, bare-hand contact is permitted when the ready-to-eat food will be subsequently cooked to at least 145 degrees F before being served.
scenario: A cook assembles raw beef patties by hand, shaping the ground beef with bare hands. The patties are then grilled to an internal temperature of 160 degrees F before serving to customers.
question: Did the cook violate the bare-hand contact rule?
